summary: For each element of a circular array, find its next greater element (searching cyclically).
mainInsight: Treat the circular array as the array concatenated with itself: two laps of a monotonic stack resolve every element, because the first lap handles elements whose greater value lies to the right and the second lap handles wraparound.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.summary: For each index scan up to n steps cyclically.

approaches.name: Monotonic stack over 2n steps
approaches.summary: Iterate i in 0..2n-1 using nums[i % n]; push indices only in the first lap.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Use nums[i % n] instead of copying the array, and only push in the first lap.

promptVariants: How do you handle the circular array?
What trick turns Next Greater Element II into the linear version?
options: Iterate twice over the array (i % n) with a monotonic stack
Sort the array first, then walk it in circular order
Reverse the array and run the same single pass over it
Binary search the maximum for each position in turn
cards.answer: Iterate twice over the array (i % n) with a monotonic stack
cards.explanation: Two laps make every element see all other elements to its right, including the wrapped ones.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search the maximum for each posit: The maximum has no answer; the rest need positional search.

promptVariants: Why are two passes enough, and why does the second pass not need to push indices?
cards.answer: An element's next greater (cyclically) is within the next n - 1 elements after it, which is covered by scanning 2n positions. On the second lap every index is already on the stack or resolved, so pushing again is unnecessary; its job is only to resolve the remaining stack entries.
cards.explanation: Your code pushes i % n on both laps, which adds redundant entries.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the two-lap monotonic stack: ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity of the two-lap monotonic stack: ___
cards.explanation: Each index is pushed once (or twice) and popped once; 2n iterations.

promptVariants: What extra memory does `circular = nums + nums` add and how can you avoid it?
How do you avoid the extra array when handling the circular case, and what is the remaining space?
cards.answer: It allocates a second array of size 2n (O(n)). Index with nums[i % n] instead and no copy is needed; the stack and answer are O(n) anyway.
cards.explanation: Total remains O(n) but with a larger constant.

promptVariants: Why `nums[stack[-1]] < circular[i]` (strict) and what happens to the elements still on the stack after the loop?
What is the answer for the maximum element?
cards.answer: Strict `<` ensures only a strictly greater value resolves an element. Elements left on the stack after two laps (the maximum and its equals) have no greater element anywhere, so they keep -1. Pushing i % n on the second lap is redundant but harmless.
cards.explanation: Equal values never resolve each other.

promptVariants: How does wraparound change the answer for the last element?
cards.explanation: The first 1 sees 2; 2 has no greater element; the last 1 wraps around to see 2.
